title: Architecture: coordination state is served, not replicated — artifact spec, served artifact reads, prose ratchet
summary: Design for the HITL-approved Option C (full remaining scope) of #3077. Six slices on a deliberately near-linear DAG: (1) R1 non-silent sync — thread per-SHA sync_to_proposals() outcomes from the wrapper into the reviewer event prompt so a failed worktree merge is never silent; (2) a declarative artifact-spec module in shared/egg_contracts — the single registry of artifact name → path template → phase → producer/consumer roles, with mandatory consistency tests against every existing hardcoding; (3) spec-derived propose-time presence validation for ALL producers, subsuming the bespoke task_planner-only validator and the refine-only _validate_producer_draft_present; (4) a strict, name-resolving gateway artifact-read endpoint (per HITL Q2: spec-registered names only, no raw-path escape hatch) modeled on gateway/contract_api.py forward-to-orchestrator, unblocking #3002; (5) phase-3 prose cleanup (REVIEWER-SYNC fetch row, event-prompt fetch-fallback prose) + docs/architecture invariant entry + the ratchet test asserting agent-facing prompt templates carry no git-sync mechanics; (6) bounded durability per HITL Q3 — fail-loud signal when BRC runs on the in-memory message-store backend plus a Redis-path restart-semantics test that distinguishes the designed _clear_concurrent_state() phase-boundary wipe from accidental mid-phase loss. The main chain is serialized (1→2→3→4→5) because slice-5 has hard file-overlap with slice-1 (event_prompt.py) and soft must-land-after edges to 3 and 4; the forest constraint forbids multi-parent, so the upstream slices are linearized per docs/architecture/slice-dag.md. Slice-6 is a parallel root (message_store.py is disjoint from every other slice).

hitl_bindings.q1_scope: Option C — full remaining scope. All six work items from the refine sketch are in.
hitl_bindings.q2_endpoint_resolution: STRICT — the artifact-read endpoint accepts only spec-registered artifact names. No raw repo-path parameter exists in the API schema at all (not merely rejected: not representable).
hitl_bindings.q3_durability_bar: Fail-loud only. EGG_MESSAGE_STORE_BACKEND=auto resolving to memory in a BRC-running deployment emits a prominent warning + health-visible flag; `auto` is NOT changed to refuse. Deeper durability stays in #3070.

runtime_primitive_assumptions.purpose: production wrapper code (generated into the consensus wrapper script)
runtime_primitive_assumptions.execution_context: in-sandbox-agent pod — runs in the per-role worktree before the agent is invoked; its only output channel today is cw_log to the wrapper log

orchestrator pod — renders the prompt the wrapper fetches; slice-1 must thread wrapper-side sync outcomes back to the orchestrator (via the event-payload round-trip or a wrapper-side prompt prepend — see recommended_approach.r1_channel) because prompt rendering happens on the other side of the HTTP boundary from the merge attempt

imported by BOTH the orchestrator pod (signals validation, prompt path rendering) and the gateway pod (artifact endpoint name resolution, phase_filter consistency); shared/ is already on both import paths (gateway/contract_api.py:34-38 inserts shared/ for egg_contracts)

called by in-sandbox-agent via GATEWAY_URL with session auth; gateway forwards to the orchestrator's authoritative repo — works on split-object-store runtimes (GKE #3002) because no agent-side object store is consulted
trusted-CI-runner pytest — scans repo files (shared/prompts/*.md, agent-facing template strings); no cluster or gateway access needed
orchestrator pod startup/first-use (_create_message_store); the health-visible flag must be readable by the existing health surface, not only the log stream

artifact_spec_module.rationale: shared/egg_contracts is already imported by both the gateway (contract_api.py) and the orchestrator; the spec must be visible to both pods plus the sandbox helper. A new sibling package would add packaging surface for no benefit.
artifact_spec_module.shape: A frozen dataclass ArtifactSpec(name, path_template, phase, producer_role, consumer_roles, description) and a module-level ARTIFACT_SPECS registry (tuple). path_template is keyed on a single '{identifier}' placeholder; the spec takes a pre-computed identifier string — _pipeline_identifier (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:928) stays where it is in this pipeline and is NOT moved (bounded scope; moving it drags pipeline-state typing into shared/). Resolution helpers: resolve_artifact_path(name, identifier) -> str; specs_for(phase=None, producer_role=None) -> tuple[ArtifactSpec, ...]; spec_by_name(name) -> ArtifactSpec | None.
artifact_spec_module.registry_note: The registry starts with the five propose-validated/served artifacts above. brc-memory and contracts are deliberately excluded: contracts are already served via the contract API (#1781) and brc-memory is wrapper-managed per-role state, not a cross-role artifact. Adding rows later is one line + the consistency test.
artifact_spec_module.consistency_tests_mandatory: Refine-risk #1 (spec-as-fourth-replica) is mitigated ONLY by tests, so they are in-slice and blocking: (a) every spec path for phase P is admitted by gateway/phase_filter.py's PhaseFileRestriction for P (and by shared/egg_restrictions/phase_patterns.py's mirror); (b) _get_draft_path('plan'/'refine', ...) output equals resolve_artifact_path('plan-draft'/'analysis-draft', identifier) for both identifier shapes (bare issue number and qualified pipeline_id, per _pipeline_identifier:936-943); (c) the prompt-prose f-string paths in routes/pipelines.py (14021, 14112 and the task_planner/risk_analyst equivalents) are rendered FROM the spec after slice-3, with an interim assertion in slice-2 that the literals match the spec.

spec_derived_validation.where: orchestrator/routes/signals.py — generalize the existing per-role validation dispatch
spec_derived_validation.design: For every CONSENSUS_PROPOSE carrying a commit_sha (no_changes_needed proposals skip, RECONSTRUCTED_NO_SHA skips): look up specs_for(phase=current_phase, producer_role=from_role); for each spec, run the existing git-show presence check (signals.py:~1195 pattern, same 15s timeout, same #3081 branch_verified semantics — reuse the existing helper, do not fork it). Roles with no registered spec for the phase (e.g. coder in implement) validate nothing — code artifacts are not draft artifacts. Plan-specific extensions (parse_plan #3026, role↔files alignment #2527/#2528) remain layered on top for the plan-draft spec only, exactly as today. _validate_producer_draft_present (refine) is deleted and subsumed; the task_planner-only entry condition at signals.py:1076-1139 becomes the generic dispatch.
spec_derived_validation.failure_mode: Same as today: positive confirmation of absence/emptiness at a locally-resolved commit raises ValueError → 400 → one cheap NACK-equivalent re-propose; all infrastructure ambiguity degrades gracefully (non-blocking), preserving the #3081 fix.

artifact_read_endpoint.gateway_route: POST /api/v1/artifact/get on a new gateway blueprint sibling to contract_api.py (same require_session_auth, same role-from-session resolution, same forward-to-EGG_ORCHESTRATOR_URL shape).
artifact_read_endpoint.orchestrator_route: A new orchestrator route module (orchestrator/routes/artifacts.py) — NOT added to signals.py or pipelines.py, keeping slice file-sets disjoint from slice-3. It resolves name → path via spec_by_name + resolve_artifact_path, then serves content via the same git show <ref>:<path> subprocess pattern as signals.py:~1195 against the orchestrator's authoritative worktree (resolve_worktree_path(pipeline_id, repo_path)).
artifact_read_endpoint.request_schema: { name: <spec-registered artifact name>, ref: <commit SHA, hex 7-64 validated — same stance as consensus_wrapper.py's SHA revalidation>, pipeline_id?: <defaults from session metadata> }. STRICT per HITL Q2: there is no path field in the schema; unregistered names → 400 with the list of registered names; non-hex refs → 400. Committed refs only — no working-tree reads (path-guessing AND staleness are both the disease).
artifact_read_endpoint.response: { ok, name, resolved_path, ref, content, truncated } with output caps consistent with existing gateway handlers (reuse the contract API's cap constants; truncated flag rather than silent cut).
artifact_read_endpoint.sandbox_helper: A small read helper in sandbox/ (CLI script consistent with existing sandbox/scripts conventions) so agents call 'artifact get <name> --ref <sha>' instead of hand-building curl; the helper is what future prompt text references.
artifact_read_endpoint.unblocks: #3002 — the rendered git-show commands in review prompts assume a shared host object store; this endpoint is the split-object-store replacement. Cross-link in the PR body and docs entry.

r1_channel.problem: The merge attempt happens wrapper-side (agent pod) AFTER the orchestrator has already rendered the event prompt — the orchestrator cannot know the outcome at render time.
r1_channel.decision: Wrapper-side prompt augmentation: sync_to_proposals() records per-SHA outcomes (merged | already-ancestor | unresolvable | merge-failed) in a local variable/temp file, and the wrapper prepends a short machine-rendered banner to the fetched prompt before invoking the agent on failure: 'WARNING: worktree NOT synced to <sha> (<reason>); treat your local diff as unreliable — use the git show commands in the delta section below.' This keeps the failure signal adjacent to the failure (same process, no new HTTP surface, no orchestrator round-trip race) and is deterministic harness bash per invariant clause 2. The alternative — POSTing outcomes back so event_prompt.py renders them — adds an orchestrator write path and a render-time ordering dependency for zero reader benefit; rejected.
r1_channel.scope_note: event_prompt.py is still touched in this slice: the empty-delta caution text (~266-281) gains a sentence pointing at the wrapper banner so the two warnings cross-reference. Test: simulated failed merge ⇒ banner text present in the agent-visible prompt.

phase3_cleanup_and_ratchet.deletions: REVIEWER-SYNC.md:110 fetch+log row (replace with: 'the wrapper has synced your worktree, or the prompt banner says it could not — the delta section carries the authoritative git show reads'); event_prompt.py ~850-880 'fetch and read the actual file diffs yourself' fallback prose (served reads + wrapper sync + slice-4 endpoint cover every consumer).
phase3_cleanup_and_ratchet.docs_invariant: New entry in docs/architecture/ (served-coordination-state): the three-clause invariant verbatim (served reads / harness-performed sync / one artifact spec), the incident lineage table from the refine analysis, and the rule that artifact paths appear in prompts only via spec rendering.
phase3_cleanup_and_ratchet.ratchet_test: A pytest scanning agent-facing prompt sources — shared/prompts/*.md and the prompt-constructing modules' emitted template strings — for sync mechanics: instructions matching git fetch/git merge/git pull as agent imperatives, and .egg-state/brc-history path references. Allowlist file with justification strings for legitimate hits (e.g. consensus_wrapper.py bash internals are harness code, not prompt prose; docs/ is out of scope). The test is writable only after the deletions, which is why it shares the slice.

bounded_durability.fail_loud: _create_message_store(): when use_redis=='auto' resolves to the in-memory fallback, escalate the existing logger.warning to a structured, unmissable signal — log at error level with a stable marker, and set a module-level flag (e.g. MESSAGE_STORE_DEGRADED) exposed through the existing orchestrator health surface so a mid-phase restart data loss is attributable post-hoc. EGG_MESSAGE_STORE_BACKEND=memory (explicit) stays quiet at warning level — explicit choice is consent. Per HITL Q3, auto is NOT changed to refuse.
bounded_durability.restart_semantics_test: Redis-path test: write BRC messages, simulate orchestrator process restart (new store instance against the same Redis), assert mid-phase messages survive; separately assert _clear_concurrent_state() still wipes at the phase boundary (the designed loss keeps happening). The two assertions in one test file so the distinction is documented where it is enforced.

slice_rationale.dag_shape: Main chain slice-1→2→3→4→5, parallel root slice-6. Forced serialization: slice-5 (cleanup+ratchet) has a HARD file-overlap edge to slice-1 (both edit orchestrator/routes/event_prompt.py — #3046) and soft must-follow edges to slice-3 and slice-4 (refine risk: reviewers on the current deploy still occasionally use the fetch fallback; delete prose only after its replacements are live). The forest constraint (one parent per slice) forbids expressing {1,3,4} as parents of 5, so per docs/architecture/slice-dag.md the upstream slices are serialized into one linear chain; serialized_chain_order is recorded on slice-5. Cost: slice-1 (R1) and slice-4 (endpoint) lose nominal parallelism with the spec chain — acceptable, both are small relative to a BRC cycle. Slice-6 touches only orchestrator/message_store.py + its tests (disjoint from all other slices' file sets) and stays a parallel root.
slice_rationale.sizing: Each slice is one coherent file-category group (wrapper+prompt / shared module / orchestrator validation / gateway+orchestrator-route+sandbox / prompts+docs+test / message-store) and should converge in ≤2 propose cycles. No slice mixes deletion-heavy work with new-API introduction (the slice-5 deletions depend on slice-1..4 introductions but live separately).

acceptance_criteria.text: A reviewer event prompt rendered after a failed sync_to_proposals() merge contains the explicit not-synced warning banner naming the SHA and reason; a successful sync renders no banner. Covered by a wrapper-side test simulating a conflicting merge.

shared/egg_contracts/artifact_spec.py exists with the five-row registry; consistency tests prove every spec path is admitted by the matching gateway phase gate AND equals _get_draft_path output for both identifier shapes. Removing/renaming any hardcoded path without updating the spec fails CI.

A propose with commit_sha from ANY refine/plan producer whose spec-registered artifact is absent/empty at the proposed commit is rejected 400 at propose time; task_planner additionally retains parse_plan + role-alignment checks; no_changes_needed and infrastructure-ambiguous cases degrade non-blocking exactly as today (#3081 semantics preserved).

POST /api/v1/artifact/get with a registered name + hex ref returns committed content with caps+truncated flag; a raw path is unrepresentable in the schema; unregistered name → 400 listing registered names; sandbox helper round-trips through the gateway with session auth. PR cross-links #3002.

REVIEWER-SYNC.md and event_prompt.py carry no agent-facing fetch/merge/pull instructions; docs/architecture entry states the three-clause invariant; the ratchet test fails when sync mechanics or brc-history paths are reintroduced into agent-facing prompt sources, with an explicit allowlist for harness-internal code.

auto→memory fallback sets a health-visible degraded flag and error-level structured log; explicit memory backend does not. Redis restart-semantics test proves mid-phase message survival across store re-instantiation AND that _clear_concurrent_state() phase-boundary wipe still occurs.

risks.risk: Spec becomes a fourth replica of path knowledge if hardcodings are left alongside it un-asserted.
risks.mitigation: Consistency tests are in-slice and blocking for slice-2 (ac-2); slice-3 re-derives the orchestrator consumers from the spec; prompt f-strings asserted in slice-2, rendered from spec by slice-3.

risks.risk: Generic file serving on the gateway becomes a policy hole.
risks.mitigation: HITL Q2 strict: name-only schema (path unrepresentable), hex-validated committed refs only, session auth + role resolution unchanged from contract_api, existing output caps reused.

risks.risk: Prose deletion regresses reviewers who still lean on the local fetch fallback.
risks.mitigation: slice-5 is last on the chain — banner (slice-1), spec (2), validation (3), endpoint (4) are all live first; REVIEWER-SYNC replacement text points at the served mechanisms.

risks.risk: Ratchet test false positives block legitimate harness-internal git text.
risks.mitigation: Scope the scan to agent-facing prompt sources only + explicit allowlist with per-entry justification; harness bash (consensus_wrapper.py internals) is out of scope by construction.

risks.risk: R1 banner channel (wrapper prepend) drifts from orchestrator prompt format.
risks.mitigation: Banner is a fixed, versioned string emitted by deterministic bash; the event_prompt empty-delta caution cross-references it; test asserts presence end-to-end in the agent-visible prompt.

risks.risk: Validation generalization breaks the #3081 graceful-degradation contract for a producer role it never covered before.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing helper (single git-show path, branch_verified semantics) rather than forking; per-role tests for refiner/architect/risk_analyst mirror the existing task_planner tests.

out_of_scope: Moving _pipeline_identifier into shared/ (spec takes identifier as input; relocation drags pipeline-state typing into shared/).
Mid-phase brc-history push/fetch or any new git distribution machinery for coordination state.
Shared worktree per phase; per-role isolation stays.
Making the prompt channel reliable; it remains lossy by design.
#3017 phase genericization (later consumes the spec; not gated here).
Message-store re-architecture beyond fail-loud + restart test (#3070 lineage).
Changing EGG_MESSAGE_STORE_BACKEND=auto to refuse BRC without Redis (explicitly rejected in HITL Q3).
